key_insight: Combining NLP predictions from radiology Findings and Impressions identified brain metastases with higher sensitivity than either section alone.
clinical_relevance: Automated report labeling could help cancer registries track brain metastases that develop after the initial cancer diagnosis.
method: Manually labeled brain/head radiology reports from a population-based Alberta cancer cohort.
Trained separate Bio_ClinicalBERT models on Findings and Impressions using 1,879 samples.
Used the higher section-level probability as the report-level prediction.
evidence_signal: Internal validation on 1,833 reports from 357 patients yielded 88.8% sensitivity and 49.9% precision at a 0.4 threshold; external sensitivity was 91.8% in Ontario and 72.6% in British Columbia.
watch_item: Modest internal precision and variable external sensitivity warrant local validation and assessment of false-positive review workload before deployment.
paper_title: Natural Language Processing Based Solution for Labeling Brain Metastasis Identified in Radiology Reports
